title: There's no need to panic (a broscientist's current crisis analysis)
summary: Off-topic reassurance video at the start of the COVID-19 crisis. NH argues no one can predict the peak, Italy's numbers can't be mapped onto the US, and the media and YouTubers (fitness ones included) are milking the crisis with clickbait. He tells viewers to consume less news and not panic.

claims.claim: Lies spread online in a crisis come from people having fun scaring others, or from scared and depressed people wanting others to feel like them.
The pandemic is serious but nothing the species hasn't seen; nobody can predict the peak, and Italy's trajectory can't simply be applied to the US's 350 million people.
He attributes northern Italy's severe outbreak to its many workers linked to Wuhan, which he says the media doesn't report.
Media audiences have been shrinking for years, so outlets milk crises for clicks; YouTube is the media in miniature, with fitness YouTubers putting the virus in titles of videos with no information.
Most people posting about the virus online are not doctors and have no inside information.
To live normally under quarantine, stop consuming so much news and online chatter, breathe, and don't panic; panicking makes it worse.
